channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: CMA will consider new SMS designation proposal, says Cardell
item.description: The UK’s Competition and Markets Authority will propose opening its fourth strategic market status investigation into a technology company under its new digital regime by the end of March, its chief executive has told lawmakers.

item.title: Google access for rival AI providers targeted in new DMA specification actions
item.description: The European Commission has launched a second round of specification proceedings under the Digital Markets Act to outline how Google must open its operating system and data to competing AI and search engine providers.

item.title: Antitrust Division gains excess HSR fees
item.description: President Donald Trump has enacted legislation that would allow the Department of Justice to keep excess merger filing fees, which the Antitrust Division estimated would lead to a 23% budget increase this year.

item.title: Mike check: The Tipline for 27 January 2026
item.description: States questioning the Hewlett Packard Enterprise/Juniper settlement are demanding texts and emails from several well-connected lobbyists who worked on the deal, including Mike Davis, who helped get Neil Gorsuch and Brett Kavanaugh confirmed to the Supreme Court and is one of the president’s staunchest defenders on social media. Also in Tipline, Ropes & Gray snags a dealmaker from Paul Weiss R...

item.title: Johnson joins Fried Frank
item.description: Fried Frank Harris Shriver & Jacobson has landed former Crowell & Moring partner Shawn Johnson, as the firm seeks to expand its antitrust team in Washington, DC.

item.title: Live issues: The Briefing for 28 January 2026
item.description: Canada’s Competition Tribunal has ordered claimants in a lawsuit seeking to break up Live Nation to amend written evidence after the specialist court rejected a separate case against Google on similar public interest grounds. Under recent amendments to the country’s competition rules, litigants can launch private abuse claims if the tribunal is satisfied the action is in the public interest, but t...

item.title: China’s Sinochem offers ‘structured’ foreign investment proposal over Pirelli stake
item.description: Chinese state-owned conglomerate Sinochem has proposed measures to mitigate foreign investment risks related to its controlling stake in Pirelli, but the company’s influence could still face scrutiny in the US and Italy.

item.title: CMA proposes first-ever conduct requirements under DMCC
item.description: News publishers and consumer groups have welcomed the UK Competition and Markets Authority’s first proposed behavioural remedies under its new digital market regime to police Google’s artificial intelligence feature in its search results, but warned content providers still need adequate remuneration.

item.title: Against the grain: The Tipline for 28 January 2026
item.description: Union Pacific’s antitrust problems do not end with its acquisition of Norfolk Southern. A lawsuit filed by farmers and a rival railroad on Tuesday accused the rail giant of monopolising shipments of grain by levying extreme fees on customers who wanted to use a more direct route. Also in Tipline, a camera technology startup accused Apple of copying and killing its product.

item.title: FTC suit ignores retailers’ sway, adhesive companies say
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission’s challenge to Henkel AG/A-Paint disregards the "significant power” of a small set of retailers to dictate which construction adhesives appear before customers, the merging parties have argued.
